rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings of the phrase mean a black muddy spring or a hot spring; both depict the sun appearing to sink at the sea horizon, and their senses can be combined.
rows.anchor: Her iki kıraat da güneşin batışı esnasında okyanusta ve başka bazı denizlerde meydana gelen manzarayı tasvir eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Dhu al-Qarnayn a powerful, learned leader with material and spiritual means, which he used in campaigns and conquests in God's cause.
rows.anchor: Zülkarneyn’i yeryüzünde güç, kuvvet, ilim, irfan ve her türlü maddî ve mânevî imkâna sahip bir lider kıldı

rows.speaker: tefsirciler
rows.claim: Commentators report that Dhu al-Qarnayn reached the Atlantic or Black Sea and watched the sun seem to set into a muddy or hot spring through sea mist; the account describes what an observer saw, not geography or cosmology.
rows.anchor: Tefsirlerde nakledildiğine göre Zülkarneyn, batıda Atlas Okyanusu’na veya Karadeniz’e kadar gitti

rows.speaker: tefsirciler
rows.claim: Commentators consider the coastal people unbelievers, which is why God left Dhu al-Qarnayn free to punish or educate and guide them kindly.
rows.anchor: Tefsircilerin kanaatine göre Zülkarneyn’in sahilde karşılaştığı kavim inkârcı bir topluluk idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing in the west, Dhu al-Qarnayn traveled east, perhaps reaching Africa's or Asia's eastern shores, the Indian Ocean, or the Caspian Sea.
rows.anchor: muhtemelen Afrika’nın veya Asya’nın doğu kıyılarına, Hint Okyanusu’na, yahut Hazar denizine ulaştı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people appear to have lived without developed civilization: they lacked clothing, houses, and vegetation that could shelter them from sun and rain.
rows.anchor: güneşin sıcağına ve yağmura karşı korunmak için ne elbise dikip giymesini biliyorlardı ne de barınabilecekleri evleri vardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran does not state the direction of the third campaign; commentators think it went north, and Kâmil Miras argues it ran south to north based on the Quran's composition.
rows.anchor: tefsirciler bunun kuzeye yapıldığı kanaatindedirler. Kâmil Miras da Zülkarneyn’in bu üçüncü seferinin güneyden kuzeye doğru gerçekleştiğini savunur

rows.speaker: Mevdûdî
rows.claim: One location proposal places the two mountains at the Derbent area among ranges extending from the Caspian toward the Black Sea, with Gog and Magog beyond them.
rows.anchor: Bir görüşe göre Zülkarneyn’in vardığı iki dağ arasından maksat Hazar denizinden Karadeniz’e doğru uzanan dağ sıraları arasında bulunan Demirkapı mıntıkasıdır

rows.speaker: Zemahşerî ve Ebüssuûd
rows.claim: Another view locates the mountains in the east, where the Turkish lands end; Elmalılı suggests this points to the Great Wall, though historians say the Chinese built it, not Dhu al-Qarnayn.
rows.anchor: meşhur Türk müfessirleri Zemahşerî ile Ebüssuûd bu kanaattedirler. Elmalılı da, “Bu görüş Çin Seddi’ne bir işarettir” diyerek konuya biraz daha açıklık getirmek istemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the mountains were eastern, they would have to be the Tien Shan and Altai, with an older barrier between them that later collapsed, rather than the Great Wall.
rows.anchor: bunların Tanrı dağları ile Altaylar, seddin de bu iki dağ arasında, Çin Seddi’nden çok daha önce yapılmış fakat zamanla yıkılmış bir set olması gerekir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading can mean the people could not understand speech or could not express it; Dhu al-Qarnayn found a way to communicate, and with their offer and help built a barrier, whose place and date the Quran leaves unspecified.
rows.anchor: kendi dillerinden başka dil bilmedikleri için Zülkarneyn’in sözlerini anlamıyorlardı veya kendi düşüncelerini ona anlatamıyorlardı

rows.speaker: tefsirciler
rows.claim: Commentaries commonly identify the people who could not understand or express speech as Turks, which would place the event in Central Asia or the Caucasus.
rows.anchor: genellikle tefsirlerde Zülkarneyn’in karşılaştığı, söz anlamayan veya anlatamayan kavmin Türkler olduğuna işaret edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran gives no information about Gog and Magog's identity, location, or era; historians call them two tribes descended from Japheth, Noah's son.
rows.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm, Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’ün kimler olduğu, nerede ve ne zaman yaşadıkları hakkında bilgi vermemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their causing corruption suggests a numerous population made up of many tribes; reports say they comprised more than twenty tribes.
rows.anchor: Yeryüzünde fesat çıkarıyorlar” meâlindeki cümle, bunların birçok kabileden meydana gelmiş kalabalık bir kitle olduklarına delâlet eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars identify Gog and Magog with destructive warrior groups of their own time, but the authors dismiss those identifications as subjective.
rows.anchor: Bir kısım âlimler, ayette geçen “Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc-ü kendi dönemlerinde savaşçı ve tamamen yıkıcı topluluklarla izah etmişler ise de bu görüşler indî değerlendirmelerdir

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says Gog and Magog try daily to breach the wall, eventually emerge when God wills, devastate people, and die from worms; animals then grow fat feeding on them.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hüreyre’den rivayet edildiğine göre Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki, “Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc her gün seddi delmeye çalışırlar

rows.speaker: İbn Kesîr
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects attribution of that hadith to the Prophet because it says they breach the wall contrary to the verse's apparent sense; he thinks Abu Hurayra likely took it from Ka'b al-Ahbar and later transmitters misattributed it.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr’e göre bu hadis Hz. Peygamber’e isnat edilemez. Zira söz konusu rivayette Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc’ün seddi delmeyi başardıkları belirtilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the wall's opening a sign near the Hour, followed by Gog and Magog's spread, the first trumpet, resurrection, and judgment.
rows.anchor: Kıyamet yaklaşınca (kıyamet alâmeti olarak) seddin açılması (Enbiyâ 21/96), Ye’cûc Me’cûc’ün yayılması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation places the wall's transformation with the first trumpet and Gog and Magog's resurrection and gathering with everyone else at the second trumpet.
rows.anchor: Birinci sûrda bütün dağlar gibi o seddin bulunduğu yerin de büyük değişime uğraması, ikinci surda diğerleri gibi Ye’cûc Me’cûc’ün de diriltilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reports about Gog and Magog cannot establish certain knowledge under Islamic rules for judging the reliability of information.
rows.anchor: İslâmî kurallara göre bunlara dayanarak kesin bir bilgiye ulaşmak mümkün değildir

rows.speaker: Orhan Kuntman
rows.claim: An allegory identifies Dhu al-Qarnayn with Muhammad, the mountains with Mecca and Medina, the barrier with Muslim unity after Mecca's conquest, and Gog and Magog with unbelievers who cannot break that unity before the Hour.
rows.anchor: Zülkarneyn Hz. Muhammed’i, Zülkarneyn’in set yaparak aralarını kapattığı iki dağ Mekke ile Medine’yi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet likened the otherwise incomprehensible trumpet to a horn; Israfil blows twice, first ending all living things and then raising them again.
rows.anchor: Sûra üflemekle görevli melek İsrâfil’dir. İki defa üfleyecek, birinci üfleyişte kâinattaki canlılar yok olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose hearts darkened through disbelief ignore signs of God's existence and power in this life, then are brought face to face with Hell in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: inkârları sebebiyle kalpleri kararmış olduğu için dünyada Allah’ın varlığını ve kudretini gösteren deliller karşısında gözlerini ve kulaklarını kapayıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verses restate the sura's central themes from its opening, using the literary device of linking the ending to the beginning; the opening praised God and the Quran, promised believers reward, and warned against associating a child with God.
rows.anchor: Arap edebiyatında konunun sonunu baş tarafıyla irtibatlandırma mânasına gelen ve “reddü’l-acez” denilen sanata güzel bir örnek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse censures worship of Jesus, angels, devils, and others besides God: no other being deserves divinity, benefits worshippers, or protects them.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı bırakıp da Hz. Îsâ’ya, meleklere, şeytanlara ve başka şeylere tapanlar kınanmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different reading allows the opening clause to be translated as asking whether taking God's servants as protectors instead of Him will benefit the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: Beni bırakıp kullarımı koruyucu edinmeleri onlara fayda verecek mi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who act well receive the gardens of Firdaus forever because they sought God's approval and acted according to His commands and pleasure.
rows.anchor: amellerini O’nun emirleri doğrultusunda ve rızâsına uygun biçimde gerçekleştirmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Firdaus can mean the finest garden, its middle or best place, a vineyard, a dense and varied orchard, or an enclosed garden.
rows.anchor: Firdevs, “bahçelerin en iyisi, bahçenin orta veya en güzel yeri, üzüm bağı, ağaçları sık ve çeşitli olan veya etrafı çevrili olan bahçe” anlamlarına gelir

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A hadith describes one hundred heavenly degrees, urges asking for Firdaus as the highest central one from which rivers flow, above which is the Merciful's throne, and says they were prepared for those striving for God.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’tan şöyle bir hadis nakledilir: “Cennette yüz derece vardır. Her derece arası, gökle yer arası kadar geniştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's words mean His infinite knowledge and wisdom; even all finite seas doubled could not supply enough ink to write them, as in Luqman 31:27.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın ilmini ve hikmetini yazmak için denizlerin tamamı mürekkep olarak kullanılsa, bir o kadar da ilâve edilse yine de Allah’ın ilmini yazmaya yeterli olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is human and cannot encompass God's knowledge; he knows only what is revealed, including the stories in this sura and the truth that all people have one God.
rows.anchor: O, sadece kendisine vahyedilenleri bilir. Bu sûredeki kıssalar ona vahyedilen ilimlerdendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone hoping to meet God should do good and worship Him without associating anyone with Him; shirk is Islam's gravest sin and God says He will not forgive it.
rows.anchor: İslâm’a göre en büyük günah Allah’a ortak koşmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Open shirk includes worshipping, seeking help from, obeying as a deity, or seeking protection from others besides God; ostentation in worship is hidden shirk, also called minor shirk in hadith.
rows.anchor: gösteriş için Allah’a ibadet etmek de gizli şirk sayılmıştır. Nitekim hadislerde bundan küçük şirk diye de bahsedilmiştir

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet said he most feared minor shirk; when companions asked, he identified it as showing off and described God directing ostentatious worshippers to seek reward from those they impressed.
rows.anchor: Sizin hakkınızda en çok korktuğum şey küçük şirktir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters at the beginning of some suras are called disconnected letters, huruf muqattaat.
rows.anchor: Bazı sûrelerin başında bulunan bu harflere “hurûf-i mukattaa” adı verilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya was among the last prophets sent to the Israelites, had no independent scripture, and followed Moses' law; sources say he was Mary's aunt's husband, Temple administrator, and copied Torah manuscripts.
rows.anchor: Zekeriyyâ aleyhisselâm, İsrâiloğulları’na gönderilmiş son peygamberlerden biridir. Ancak kendisine müstakil bir kitap verilmemiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quiet, humble, pleading prayer best fits its etiquette; Zakariya feared his relatives would fail to lead the community and spread God's religion, so he sought a virtuous, capable, just successor from himself and Jacob's line, never despairing of God.
rows.anchor: alçak sesle ve yalvarıp yakararak yapılması onun âdâbına daha uygun olduğu için alçak sesle dua ettiği belirtilen Hz. Zekeriyyâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wali, translated as successor, can mean a person's relative, friend, companion, helper, or supporter; the word also names God and has other senses discussed in linked verses.
rows.anchor: velî kelimesi, kişinin “yakını, dostu, arkadaşı, yardımcı ve destekçisi” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mawali means inheriting close relatives; Zakariya sought a successor to propagate religion, not for pride or personal gain, and prayed elsewhere for pure offspring and not to be left childless.
rows.anchor: mevlâ kelimesinin çoğulu olup “kişiye vâris olan yakın akrabaları” mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentaries say Zakariya sought a child inheriting property, knowledge, and prophethood; the authors reject property inheritance based on the hadith that prophets leave charity, interpreting the inheritance as Israel's prophetic mission, tradition, and ethics.
rows.anchor: Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın “Tarafından bana yerimi alacak bir halef ver; o, Ya‘kub hânedanına da vâris olsun” ifadesi de bu mânayı destekler

rows.speaker: İbn Âşûr
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur reads the verses as permitting inheritance from prophets, supported by 27:16, and says the hadith referred only to Muhammad; Umar also said the Prophet meant himself.
rows.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre âyetlerin zâhirinden peygamberlere mirasçı olunabileceği anlaşılmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted Zakariya's prayer and announced Yahya's birth, as also noted at 21:90.
rows.anchor: Yüce Allah, Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın duasını kabul etti ve Yahyâ adında bir oğlunun olacağını ona müjdeledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samiyy can mean named or similar; commentators prefer named because calling Yahya unmatched would imply superiority to earlier great prophets such as Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: Tefsirciler, böyle bir anlayış Yahyâ’nın, kendisinden önceki Hz. İbrâhim ve Hz. Mûsâ gibi büyük peygamberlerden de üstün olmasını gerektireceği için birinci mânayı tercih etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No earlier prophet combined Yahya's traits: birth to elderly parents, his unprecedented name, and wisdom in childhood, understood as prophethood or grasp of scripture.
rows.anchor: onun ihtiyar bir baba ile kısır ve yaşlı bir anneden dünyaya gelmesi, Yahyâ adının ondan önce hiç kimseye verilmemiş olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was also called master and prophet, specially guarded in chastity, ascetic, and herald of Jesus' mission; these distinctions do not make him absolutely the greatest prophet.
rows.anchor: bu meziyetler onun mutlak mânada en üstün peygamber olduğunu değil, anılan niteliklerden dolayı farklı olduğunu ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya wanted a spiritual successor rather than specifically a child, so he expressed surprise when promised a son.
rows.anchor: Hz. Zekeriyyâ özellikle çocuk değil, kendisine mânen vâris olacak bir halef istemişti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three nights without speech here and three days in Aal Imran include their corresponding days or nights; Zakariya could gesture and was told to glorify God morning and evening.
rows.anchor: Şu halde burada geceler gündüzleriyle birlikte, Âl-i İmrân’da ise günler geceleriyle birlikte kastedilmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating a child from elderly parents is easy for the Creator who made Adam from earth and makes things by saying Be, as in 36:82.
rows.anchor: bir şeyi yaratmak istediği zaman “ol” der, hemen oluverir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mihrab means a private worship place where Zakariya prayed; for communal worship he went to Bayt al-Maqdis, and the good news of his son came in the private place.
rows.anchor: mihrâb, “özel ibadet yeri” anlamına gelmektedir. Burada Zekeriyyâ’nın özel ibadet ve dualarını yaptığı yeri ifade eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya left his worship place, approached his people, and gestured that they glorify God morning and evening.
rows.anchor: işaret yoluyla onlardan sabah akşam Allah’ı anmalarını, O’nu tesbih etmelerini istemiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya received no separate book; he was told to understand and follow the Torah revealed to Moses.
rows.anchor: Yahyâ’ya herhangi bir kitap indirilmemiş, ancak Hz. Mûsâ’ya indirilmiş olan Tevrat’ı iyi anlayıp onunla amel etmesi emredilmiştir

rows.speaker: Şevkânî
rows.claim: Shawkani explains childhood wisdom as grasping the commanded book and religious rulings, while also listing knowledge, acting on knowledge, prophethood, and intellect as possible senses.
rows.anchor: Şevkânî, Yahyâ’ya daha çocukken verilen hikmeti, “kendisine sımsıkı sarılması emredilen kitabı kavrama, dinî hükümleri anlama yeteneği” şeklinde açıklamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created Yahya with pure nature: he was compassionate, reverent, devoted, dutiful to parents, attentive to people's rights, and free of tyranny and disobedience.
rows.anchor: O, insanlara karşı son derecede şefkatli, Allah’a karşı saygılı, dinine bağlı, ana-babasına iyilik eden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another verse describes Yahya as affirming God's scripture, chaste, noble, and a righteous prophet.
rows.anchor: onun, Allah’ın kitabını tasdik eden, iffetli, asil ve sâlih bir peygamber olduğu ifade buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya's seven virtues are wisdom, compassion, purity, piety, respect for parents, freedom from tyranny, and obedience; God's care accompanies him at birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: bütün bu hallerde yani dünyaya gelirken, dünyadan giderken ve kıyamet gününde kabirden kalkarken Allah’ın inâyetinin onunla beraber olacağı bildirilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative moves from Zakariya and Yahya to Mary, the sura's central subject; Mary had been dedicated to the Temple before birth, worshipped in seclusion behind a screen, and the eastern side means Jerusalem's Bayt al-Maqdis.
rows.anchor: 16. âyette ifade edilen doğu tarafından maksat Kudüs’teki Beyt-i Makdis’in doğu tarafıdır

rows.speaker: tefsirciler
rows.claim: Commentators identify the sent spirit as Gabriel; unable to perceive the angel in his true form, Mary saw him as a well-formed man, feared harm, then asked how a virgin could bear a child.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler 17. âyette Allah tarafından gönderildiği bildirilen “ruh”un Cebrâil olduğu kanaatindedirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created Jesus without a father as a sign of divine power and appointed him prophet as a mercy to people; creation is easy for God, as in Aal Imran 3:45–47 and 3:59.
rows.anchor: Hz. Îsâ’yı baba faktörü olmaksızın yaratmış ve insanlar için bir rahmet olsun diye onu peygamber olarak görevlendirmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary conceived when God caused the spirit to be breathed through an angel, as also stated in 21:91 and 66:12.
rows.anchor: Allah melek vasıtasıyla ruhu üfleyince Meryem hamile kaldı

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Commentaries report gestation periods ranging from one hour to nine months; Ibn Kathir says most held it was nine months.
rows.anchor: Tefsirlerde hamilelikle ilgili olarak bir saat ile dokuz ay arasında farklı sürelerden söz edilmiş olmakla birlikte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew to a distant place and concealed the pregnancy for a time because she feared people's reproach.
rows.anchor: insanların kendisini kınayacağından endişe ettiği için, durumu ailesinden gizlemek maksadıyla uzak bir yere çekilerek bir müddet hamileliğini gizledi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As labor began, Mary sheltered beneath a palm tree and feared people would reject her innocence, despite previously knowing her as virtuous; grief made her wish to die and be forgotten.
rows.anchor: insanların kendisinin günahsız olduğunu kabul etmeyeceklerini düşünerek tedirgin oluyordu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God consoles Mary by providing spring water to drink and fresh dates to eat.
rows.anchor: onun için çıkardığı kaynak suyundan içecek, meyve vermesini sağladığı hurmadan da yiyecektir

rows.speaker: Şevkânî
rows.claim: Shawkani says the phrase rendered as a spring beneath her could instead mean that Jesus was brought forth from her.
rows.anchor: “Senden Îsâ’yı yaratıp çıkarmıştır” şeklinde çevirmek de mümkündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aaron addressed is not Moses' prophet brother; one view says Mary had a brother named Aaron who was virtuous like their parents, so people found misconduct by his sister inconceivable.
rows.anchor: Kimine göre Hz. Meryem’in Hârûn adında bir kardeşi vardı. Ana babası gibi o da iffetli ve sâlih bir kimse idi

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A prophetic report explains that Israelites named children after earlier prophets and righteous people, which is why Mary's brother was called Aaron.
rows.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’den rivayet edilen bir hadiste de, İsrâiloğulları’nda önceki peygamberlerin ve iyi kimselerin isimlerini çocuklarına ad koyma geleneği olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says Mary was addressed as Aaron's sister because she descended from the prophet Aaron.
rows.anchor: Meryem’in peygamber olan Hârûn’un soyundan gelmiş olması münasebetiyle kendisine böyle hitap edilmiş olduğudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary answered the accusation by pointing to Jesus; the people marveled at speaking to an infant, who then spoke.
rows.anchor: olayı çocukla konuşmaları için ona işaret etti. Fakat onlar, “Beşikteki bebekle nasıl konuşalım?!” diyerek hayretlerini ifade ettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus first declares himself God's servant, not a deity or part of a trinity, and a prophet; he must perform worship, was born, will die and be raised like others, and his words imply prayer existed among prophets after Abraham despite differences in form.
rows.anchor: Böylece Hz. Îsâ kendisinin bir ilâh değil bir kul ve bir peygamber olduğunu, ilâhî varlığın üç öğesinden biri olmadığını ilân etmiş oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book given to Jesus is the Gospel; Shawkani's reading that he became prophet and received scripture at that moment is weak, since the infant was announcing God's eternal decree for him.
rows.anchor: bu yorum zayıf bulunmuştur. Bu sözden, daha bebek iken yaptığı konuşmada Allah’ın ezelde kendisi için peygamberliği ve kitap verilmesini takdir ettiğini açıklamasının istendiği anlaşılmaktadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus mentions duty to honor his mother rather than parents because he had no father; Quran accordingly calls him Jesus son of Mary.
rows.anchor: Hz. Îsâ babasız olarak bakire bir anadan dünyaya geldiği için, “Allah beni ana babama saygılı olmayı emretti” dememiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage summarizes Jesus as God's servant and prophet, blessed everywhere, obligated to worship, respectful to his mother, neither tyrannical nor disobedient.
rows.anchor: 30-33. âyetlerde Hz. Îsâ’nın başlıca nitelikleri şöyle sıralanmaktadır

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: One interpretation says the account of Jesus son of Mary is true and gives the truth about which people dispute.
rows.anchor: “İşte hakkında şüphe ettikleri Meryem oğlu Îsâ ile ilgili olarak bu anlatılanlar doğrudur. Gerçek söz budur”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading rejects both Jewish claims that Jesus was illegitimate and Christian claims that he was God's son; he is God's word and spirit, while God alone is the true deity and should be worshipped.
rows.anchor: Hz. Îsâ hakkında yahudilerin “O, gayri meşrû ilişkiden dünyaya gelmiştir” şeklindeki sözleri doğru olmadığı gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading treats Jesus' infant declaration as the true word: assigning God a child is false, and people wrongly dispute rather than accept Jesus as servant and messenger.
rows.anchor: Gelecek olan Hz. Îsâ’nın, daha sabi iken bir mûcize eseri olarak dile gelip ilân ettiği gerçek sözdür

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: Commentators identify the disputing parties as Jews and Christians or Christian sects: Jews deny Jesus as prophet, most Christians call him God's son and deity, and a small group calls him God's servant and messenger.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler, 37. âyette Hz. Îsâ hakkında ayrılığa düştükleri belirtilen grupların, yahudilerle hıristiyanlar veya Hıristiyanlık’taki farklı mezhep mensupları olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meşhed means seeing or witnessing and can denote a place or time of either; the verse may curse unbelievers at the great day or where, when, or because witnesses testify against them.
rows.anchor: Meşhed kelimesi sözlükte “görmek veya şahitlik etmek” demektir. Yer veya zaman ismi olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who rejected monotheism and strayed from truth in this life will see and hear it fully when they appear before God.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın huzuruna çıkacakları gün onu bütün açıklığı ile işitecek ve göreceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the day of regret the sudden Hour, ending worldly responsibility while people are heedless; the Prophet is told to warn them beforehand of regret over sins and omitted good deeds.
rows.anchor: Maksat kıyamet günüdür. İnsanlar gaflet içinde, Allah’ın dinine inanmaz ve dünya tutkusuyla âhireti düşünmezlerken birden bire kıyamet kopar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes it the reckoning day, when rewards and punishments are announced and people are separated for Paradise or Hell; unbelievers regret losing eternal life.
rows.anchor: Pişmanlık gününden maksat hesap günüdür. O gün herkesin hesabı görülmüş, sevap ve cezaları açıklanmak suretiyle iş bitirilmiş olacaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean that only God is permanent while the world passes, or that after the trumpet all living things die, ownership ends, and everything returns to its true owner.
rows.anchor: Dünya ve üzerinde bulunan her şey geçicidir, hiçbir gücün desteğine muhtaç olmaksızın kalıcı olan yalnız Allah’tır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abraham story warns Arabs who claim descent from a monotheist and Kaaba-building ancestor yet abandoned his religion for idols; Quraysh honored Abraham but inflicted similar persecution on Muhammad.
rows.anchor: Kureyşliler Hz. İbrâhim’i dinî önderleri olarak kabul ediyor ve onun soyundan gelmekle iftihar ediyorlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although called a prophet here, Abraham is elsewhere said to receive scriptures, showing that he was both prophet and messenger.
rows.anchor: başka âyetlerde ona sahifeler gönderildiği ifade buyurulmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham repeatedly addressed his father Azar respectfully as my father despite his idolatry and threats; the passage shows a younger person may advise an elder and that true religious guidance comes from revelation.
rows.anchor: Hz. İbrâhim, babası Âzer’e her sözünün başında “babacığım” diye hitap etmekte

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obeying Satan against God's command counts as worshipping him; Quran calls conduct against reason, truth, and ethics satanic and conscious surrender to it worship, as Esed notes.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın emrine aykırı olmasına rağmen şeytanın emrine itaat etmek, “ona tapma” olarak değerlendirilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham promised to seek forgiveness before learning his father would die an unbeliever and enemy of God; then he stopped praying for him.
rows.anchor: Bu durumu öğrenince babasının affı için dua etmekten vazgeçti

rows.speaker: tefsirci ve tarihçiler
rows.claim: Commentators and historians say Abraham migrated through Harran, Palestine, Egypt, then back to Palestine with Sarah, Lot, and Lot's wife; Lot settled in Sodom and Gomorrah, while Abraham remained in Palestine.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim aleyhisselâm Allah yolunda hicret ederek önce Harran’a, sonra Filistin’e, buradan da Mısır’a gitmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted elderly Abraham and Sarah Isaac, then Isaac's son Jacob, making them prophets; later Israelite prophets descended from them, while Ishmael, Abraham's first son by Hagar, became ancestor of the Hijaz Arabs.
rows.anchor: Burada kendisi ve eşi Sâre yaşlanmış oldukları halde Allah onlara oğulları İshak’ı lutfetti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lisān sidq may mean their truthful, elevated speech, or their good reputation; Abraham prayed to be remembered well and God granted it, directing Muhammad to follow his religion, so Muslims and People of the Book honor him and his descendants.
rows.anchor: Bu tamlama onların, “doğruluktan yana üstün bilinmeleri yani iyi anılmaları” anlamına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' story is the fourth account; sent to Israel, he is among the great steadfast prophets for those who understand ulu al-azm as the five greatest prophets.
rows.anchor: “ülü’l-azim” tabirini büyük peygamberler (daha çok beş büyük peygamber) anlamında kabul edenlere göre o da bu gruptaki peygamberlerden biridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhlas can mean chosen and specially favored; the authors consider that fitting because God selected Moses to speak with Him and made him prophet; the muhlis reading means sincere worship solely for God.
rows.anchor: Muhlis şeklindeki kıraate göre bu kelime, “ibadeti yalnız Allah için yapan, O’na tahsis eden” mânasına gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Moses received the Torah, he is called both messenger and prophet.
rows.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’ya Tevrat indirilmiş olduğu için burada ona hem resul hem de nebî denilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain was Sinai; Tur is used alone eight times for Sinai, also named Tur Sinai at 23:20 and Tur Sinin at 95:2.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’da Sînâ dağı, ilkinde “Tûri Seynâe” (Mü’minûn 23/20), ikincisinde “Tûri Sînîn” (Tîn 95/2) şeklinde olmak üzere iki defa geçer

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: The mountain's right side means the side to Moses' right as he faced it, since a mountain has no intrinsic right or left; God called to Moses from that side.
rows.anchor: Tûr’un sağ tarafı”ndan maksat Hz. Mûsâ’nın yüzünü Tûr’a dağına döndürdüğünde bulunduğu yerin sağ tarafıdır

rows.speaker: Şevkânî
rows.claim: An alternative takes eyman as blessed, so God called to Moses from the mountain's blessed side; the authors prefer spiritual nearness over a claim that Moses physically heard the pen scratching the tablets, and Ibn Ashur calls nearness a metaphor for revelation.
rows.anchor: “sağ taraf” diye tercüme ettiğimiz eymen kelimesi “bereketli” (mübarek) anlamına gelmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's nearness means spiritual rank, not physical closeness; a sacred hadith describes a servant's nearness to God through obligatory and voluntary worship and resulting moral elevation.
rows.anchor: “Allah onu mânevî makam bakımından kendisine yaklaştırdı” diye tefsir edenler de vardır ve bu mâna daha uygun görünmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At God's instruction to confront Pharaoh for Israel's release, Moses asked for Aaron as prophet and helper; God granted this, and eloquent Aaron spoke for Moses, whose speech was impeded, and deputized for him.
rows.anchor: Allah Teâlâ onun duasını kabul ederek kardeşini de peygamber olarak görevlendirdi ve onun yanına yardımcı olarak verdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was exemplary in keeping promises, urged his family to pray and give zakat, and earned God's approval through gratitude, beauty of character, and submission; Muhammad was also commanded to order family prayer and persist in it.
rows.anchor: Hz. İsmâil ahde vefa erdemiyle temayüz etmiş bir kimseydi, sözünde durmaya özen gösterirdi

rows.speaker: tefsirciler
rows.claim: Commentators say Idris was originally named Uhnuh, Noah's third-generation ancestor, and received prophethood with thirty revealed pages after Seth.
rows.anchor: Tefsircilerin belirttiğine göre, İdrîs’in asıl adı Uhnûh olup Hz. Nûh’un üçüncü batından dedesidir

rows.speaker: Ömer Faruk Harman
rows.claim: A shared tradition in scriptural religions calls Idris the first founder of knowledge, civilization, and rational systems, crediting him with sciences, crafts, agriculture, ironwork, writing, sewing, and related discoveries.
rows.anchor: Kitaplı dinlerde ortak rivayet ve inanışa göre İdrîs ilmin, medeniyetin ve aklî sistemlerin ilk kurucusudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being raised to a high station may refer to Idris's achievements or to an exceptional place in the spiritual realm or heavens, supported by reports.
rows.anchor: Bu ifadeyi, onun mânevî âlemde (göklerde) müstesna yerlerde bulunduğu şeklinde anlamak da mümkündür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Of the eleven distinguished figures named in the sura, all except Mary were prophets; Mary was a chosen woman and mother of Jesus, praised repeatedly in the Quran.
rows.anchor: adları geçen ve kıssaları anlatılan on bir seçkin şahıstan Hz. Meryem hariç hepsi peygamberlik şerefine ermiş kimselerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The figures' lineage runs through Adam, Shem son of Noah, Abraham, or Israel: Idris from Adam; Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob from Abraham; Moses, Aaron, Zakariya, and Yahya from Israel; and Jesus through his mother.
rows.anchor: Bunların hepsi genelde Âdem’in soyundandır. Özelde ise İdrîs, Hz. Âdem’in soyundan; İbrâhim, Hz. Nûh ile birlikte gemiye binen oğlu Sâm’ın soyundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All were guided, chosen, sincere servants who prostrated at God's verses and wept from spiritual sensitivity.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın âyetleri okunduğunda derhal secdeye kapanacak kadar itaatkâr ve göz yaşı dökecek kadar duyarlı insanlardır
